The conflicts are inflated by stale stacked-PR ancestry, not 48 unrelated problems.

[PR #570](https://github.com/21nCo/nucleum/pull/570) was created as “PR 4 of 9” on top of #569. Since then, #567, #568, and #569 were merged into `dev` with different commit SHAs and several review-fix commits. PR #570 was retargeted to `dev` without rebasing its branch onto those merged versions.

Current state:

- `dev`: `9971f77`
- PR head: `e28a581`
- Common ancestor: `6972371`
- `dev` changed 141 files after that ancestor.
- PR #570 changed 153 files.
- 91 files were changed on both sides.
- Result: 48 conflict files—25 content, 18 add/add, and 5 modify/delete.

Critically, `git cherry` shows that the PR’s first five commits are patch-equivalent to work already merged into `dev`. Only these two commits are genuinely new:

- `3081b71f` — Replace legacy client persistence with DataFn runtime
- `e28a5819` — Migrate web authentication to AuthFn client

So Git is trying to merge two differently reviewed versions of the same DataFn/AuthFn foundation. The review fixes on `dev` also deliberately modified legacy persistence and store files that #570 later removes or rewrites.

The clean resolution is to rebuild/rebase #570 onto current `dev`, replaying only those final two commits. A net-delta simulation reduces the conflict set from 48 files to 9: five real content conflicts and four intentional delete-vs-modify decisions. Manually resolving all 48 on the current ancestry would be unnecessary and risk reintroducing superseded predecessor code.
proceed with the recommended approach and also resolve the remaining conflicts

I’ll use the `create-pr-ghother` workflow because this PR branch is not the current checkout and needs a clean, exact-head worktree. I’ll rebuild #570 onto live `dev`, replay only its two genuine commits, resolve the nine semantic conflicts against the predecessor review fixes, run targeted validation, then force-update the existing PR branch with a lease.

The workflow confirms the current checkout is clean but on a backup branch, so I’m leaving it untouched. The repository has no `CONTRIBUTING.md`; I’ve read the available `README.md` and `WARP.md`, and I’m now pinning the live `dev` and PR heads before creating the isolated rebuild worktree.

The first genuine commit produces eight conflicts: four legacy persistence deletions and four store integrations. This matches the earlier prediction. I’m resolving them against the review-fix intent on `dev`, especially the staged-runtime and legacy product-key protections, rather than automatically taking either side.

const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd: "set -euo pipefail
snapshot_dir=/tmp/pr570-review-snapshot-2e46d625.tedGCp
export GH_CONFIG_DIR=/Users/serro/.config/gh-other
cursor=$(jq -r '.[-1].data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.endCursor' "$snapshot_dir/thread-pages.json")
page=2
while [[ "$cursor" != "null" ]]; do
  gh api graphql -F endCursor="$cursor" -f query='query($endCursor: String) {
    repository(owner: "21nCo", name: "nucleum") {
      pullRequest(number: 570) {
        reviewThreads(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
          nodes {
            id
            isResolved
            path
            line
            originalLine
            startLine
            originalStartLine
            comments(first: 100) {
              nodes {
                id
                databaseId
                body
                author { login }
                createdAt
                updatedAt
                outdated
                url
                path
                line
                originalLine
                diffHunk
                commit { oid }
                originalCommit { oid }
                replyTo { id }
              }
              pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
            }
          }
          pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
        }
      }
    }
  }' > "$snapshot_dir/thread-page-$page.json"
  has_next=$(jq -r '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage' "$snapshot_dir/thread-page-$page.json")
  print -r -- "thread_page=$page nodes=$(jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes|length' "$snapshot_dir/thread-page-$page.json") hasNextPage=$has_next"
  if [[ "$has_next" != "true" ]]; then
    cursor=null
  else
    cursor=$(jq -r '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.endCursor' "$snapshot_dir/thread-page-$page.json")
  fi
  page=$((page + 1))
done
jq -s '.[0] + .[1:]' "$snapshot_dir/thread-pages.json" "$snapshot_dir"/thread-page-*.json > "$snapshot_dir/thread-pages-complete.json"
jq '[.[] | .data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]]' "$snapshot_dir/thread-pages-complete.json" > "$snapshot_dir/threads.json"
overflow=$(jq '[.[] | select(.comments.pageInfo.hasNextPage == true)] | length' "$snapshot_dir/threads.json")
if [[ "$overflow" != "0" ]]; then
  print -u2 -- "thread comment pagination overflow=$overflow"
  exit 42
fi
head_sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cutoff_epoch=$(git show -s --format=%ct HEAD)
jq -n \
  --arg snapshotDir "$snapshot_dir" \
  --arg head "$head_sha" \
  --argjson cutoffEpoch "$cutoff_epoch" \
  --slurpfile threads "$snapshot_dir/threads.json" \
  --slurpfile reviews "$snapshot_dir/reviews.json" \
  --slurpfile issueComments "$snapshot_dir/issue-comments.json" \
  --slurpfile inlineComments "$snapshot_dir/inline-comments.json" \
  '{snapshotDir:$snapshotDir, head:$head, cutoffEpoch:$cutoffEpoch,
    threads:($threads[0]|length),
    unresolved:([$threads[0][]|select(.isResolved==false)]|length),
    unresolvedCurrentHead:([$threads[0][]|select(.isResolved==false)|.comments.nodes[-1]|select(.outdated==false and .commit.oid==$head)]|length),
    threadCommentOverflow:([$threads[0][]|select(.comments.pageInfo.hasNextPage==true)]|length),
    reviews:($reviews[0]|length),
    issueComments:($issueComments[0]|length),
    inlineComments:($inlineComments[0]|length),
    newReviews:([$reviews[0][]|select((.submitted_at|fromdateiso8601)>$cutoffEpoch)]|length),
    newIssueComments:([$issueComments[0][]|select((.created_at|fromdateiso8601)>$cutoffEpoch)]|length),
    newInlineComments:([$inlineComments[0][]|select((.created_at|fromdateiso8601)>$cutoffEpoch)]|length)}' | tee "$snapshot_dir/summary.json"",
  workdir: "/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus-pr-570-review",
